title: object and companion object
context: What is the difference between an object declaration, a companion object and a top-level function?

refs.title: Atomic Kotlin (book) by Bruce Eckel & Svetlana Isakova

answer: An `object` declaration is a singleton: one instance, created lazily on first use. A companion object lives inside a class, and its members are accessed as `ClassName.member`. Each class has at most one companion, and it can implement interfaces. A top-level function has no owner and no state. Use a companion for factory functions and constants tied to a class, and a top-level function for stateless helpers.

points.title: Singleton object
points.why: An object declaration gives one shared instance.

points.title: Companion access
points.why: Companion members look like static members through the class name.
